name: API and CPI oily-water separators
principle: First step of a refinery effluent train: free (non-emulsified) oil floats under gravity in a long, baffled API-type basin designed to API 421, or coalesces on tilted corrugated plates (CPI/PPI), which pack the same duty into a smaller footprint. Skimmed oil is recovered; the oily water continues to flotation (DAF/IGF) and then biological treatment. IPIECA's refinery train: API separator, then DAF or IAF, then equalisation and biological treatment.

performance.metric: free-oil droplet removal threshold, API separator
performance.basis: API 421: traditional separators remove only down to about 150-micron droplets under ideal conditions
designed to produce an effluent of 100 mg/L or less of oil droplets 150 micron and larger, non-emulsified free oil

advantages: The signature first step of an industrial effluent train; recovers oil as a product
CPI packs the duty into a smaller footprint than an API basin
limitations: Removes only free oil — emulsified and soluble organics need flotation and biological treatment
Separator bottom sludge is a listed hazardous waste in many regimes
